text:
maya: Quick proposal — staggered spot-reshuffle + client-side bearer-swap for long-lived streaming sessions. On preemptible evict (30s notice) server marks session 'handoff_pending', emits short-lived swap token + grace-window, then drains active request queue while clients swap tokens and reconnect to fallback pool.

kenji: sounds promising. main concerns: KV cache continuity, in-flight requests being double-processed, and warmed-up duplicates inflating GPU load. what drain duration are you thinking?

maya: baseline: drain=8s + 22s reconnect/catchup to match typical 30s eviction. adaptive: if pending_requests > 50 => drain=8s else drain=3s.

alex: how do we ship token? proto event vs Authorization header? also redact from logs.

maya: short-lived bearer: `Authorization: Bearer HANDOFF-<sess>-<seq>-<hmac>`. client calls `/swap` with it, server validates and returns new endpoint. log only sess+seq (no hmac).

serena: dedupe is critical. if old node requeues and new node also requeues same req we get duplicates. need request_uuid + attempt_count + dedupe TTL.

kenji: agree. runtime accepts requeue only if attempt_count < MAX_ATTEMPTS. dedupe cache TTL=60s. use memcached or local LRU keyed by request_uuid -> last_attempt_ts.

maya: KV continuity: include tiny prefix checkpoint in handoff metadata: last_kv_prefix_seq + optional snapshot_ref. fallback can warm KV by replaying deltas starting from prefix_seq. cost vs quality tradeoff.

alex: snapshot_ref might mean ephemeral snapshot storage per session — expensive. alternative: client supplies last_tokenized_prefix_hash and server replays missing tokens.

serena: client-replay is simpler but clients (mobile) may not preserve history. fallback: if client can't provide prefix, run stateless lower-quality mode or route to dedicated pool for SLO-critical requests.

ops-bot: eviction-simulator ran 10 trials for proposal: avg failover 1.9s, median 1.7s, tail 6.1s. logs: "handoff issued, swap accepted, KV-warmup started" :white_check_mark:

kenji: warming can spike GPU when both nodes handle batches. add soft-rate-limit on warmup: warmup_qps = min(10% capacity, 500 qps). throttle warmup tokens, prioritize active producers.

maya: and circuit-breaker: if warmup_qps > threshold for >10s, fallback hot-traffic to dedicated pool to protect SLOs.

alex: implementation checklist: 1) handoff token gen/validate 2) client swap endpoint + SDK hook 3) request_uuid propagation + dedupe layer 4) KV prefix metadata + client replay path 5) warmup rate-limit + dedicated fallback 6) observability (per-session handoffs, warmup_qps, double-run rate).

serena: tests: simulate 500 concurrent streaming sessions with 10% preempt probability, measure tail latency, double-run rate, and cost delta. chaos test swap message loss to verify requeue correctness.

maya: i'll open RFC with checklist + API spec, tag eng-runtime and oncall for review. @kenji @alex please add notes in RFC by EOD.

kenji: will add notes. :thumbsup:

alex: prototype SDK swap hook tomorrow.

serena: drafting test harness scenarios.

maya: thanks all — filing RFC now.
